# Alibre Design C++ Add-On Template

- This is a C++ starter project for an Alibre Design add-on, giving you a working add-on you can rename and fill in with your own code.
  - What it does
    - Builds a native 64-bit add-on DLL that Alibre Design can load.
    - Implements the full add-on interface, covering menus, commands, saving state, and licensing hooks.
    - Ships one working sample command that draws a textured triangle into the Alibre 3D window.
    - Adds a menu with a Post Render and an Override Render command so you can compare the two approaches.
    - Includes a test part and a texture image so the sample runs straight away.
  - What you need
    - Alibre Design installed, so the add-on can be loaded and tested.
    - Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ desktop workload.
    - The legacy DirectX SDK, because the sample links against it.
  - Getting started
    - Build `source/ADSampleAddOnDX.sln` in Release configuration for x64.
    - Copy the build output into your Alibre Design add-ons directory.
    - Start Alibre Design, open the test part, and run the DX Triangle commands.
    - Rename the project, the descriptor, and the identifier, then replace the sample command with your own.
  - Where things live
    - `source/` holds the C++ project, the add-on descriptor, and the sample assets.
    - `documentation/` holds reference notes.
  - Good to know
    - Give your add-on a fresh identifier before you ship it, so it does not clash with the sample.
  - Use it under the MIT License.
